description:
Problem: when a Trunk run on develop goes red, make trunk-status and make pr-open name the culprit (#3433). The arm gate refuses new arming from the first red run of the streak (#3415). But PRs armed before the red run completed still merge (docs/internal/develop-post-merge-gaps.md:75-78). After PR 3185 merged on 2026-10-20, develop stayed red about 39 minutes before anyone acted. The linked-worktree revert failure seen then was fixed by #3220.

Outcome: a workflow triggered on completion of a Trunk run on develop. For each open PR against develop with auto-merge enabled, it evaluates the same decision as scripts/trunk_revert.py arm-gate and disables auto-merge exactly when arm-gate would refuse that PR, treating an arm-gate error as a refusal. It never arms or re-arms; after develop is green or the revert merges, authors re-arm with make pr-arm. It logs each disarmed PR with the culprit and run URL.

Not in scope (owner setting): blocking merges made through the GitHub UI or raw gh pr merge needs a required status check on develop that fails while Trunk is red. That is an owner decision; if the owner wants it, file a separate item for the status producer, and the owner adds the context.

Decision gates:
1. Predicate reuse. The disarm decision calls the arm-gate logic in scripts/trunk_revert.py; it does not reimplement it. The culprit's genuine revert PR, and any PR the arm gate admits, stay armed. Stop if reuse needs a second definition of the red streak.
2. Trigger and trust. workflow_run on the Trunk workflow, branch develop, running the default-branch workflow file. Permissions: pull-requests write, actions read, contents read; nothing else. Stop and ask the owner if it needs any other write permission or a secret.
3. Idempotence. Repeated red runs and re-runs disarm nothing twice and touch no unarmed PR. A green completion does nothing.

Item guardrails: the workflow never enables auto-merge, never adds or removes labels, never closes, comments on, rebases or re-runs PRs, and never edits rulesets. It is a soundness path, so it needs the oracle's review.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings in code; commits, PR bodies and docs carry no tracker item IDs or session labels; timing uses benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time().
